messages:
Alex: Heads-up: I'm prototyping a per-tenant 'token-watermark' admission policy to replace the reservoir model we've been using. Idea is to keep a single running watermark (tokens/sec equivalent) per tenant with exponential decay + a spike budget. Admit if current rate < watermark or if spike budget is available. Thoughts? :thinking:

Mira: Short question — what's the main operational win vs reservoir? Is this mainly to reduce state + make fairness more responsive?

Alex: Yup. Reservoirs are bursty and require more bookkeeping (multiple buckets, leases). Watermark is one float + last-updated ts, cheaper to shard and easier to reason about long-tail abuse. Decay means tenants that stop traffic recover naturally.

Chen: How does this touch priority/reserved tenants? We need a clear interface boundary. Do we apply watermark before priority scoring or after we compute admission score?

Sam: My vote: run admission (watermark) before priority allocation so we protect headroom for high-priority tenants. But we must expose an exception hook so platform/enterprise tenants can request temporary overrides (subject to audit).

Mira: Telemetry requirements: per-tenant counters: watermark value over time, admissions_allowed/denied, spike_budget_used. Also global fairness signals (Gini or p99 rejection rate across tenants) to detect systemic drift.

Alex: Draft config example for discussion:
```
watermark_policy:
  default_spike_budget: 1000        # tokens
  spike_decay_window_s: 60         # exponential decay half-life
  min_watermark: 1.0               # lower clamp
  max_watermark: 10000             # upper clamp
  exception_roles: ["enterprise", "dedicated"]
```

Chen: Edge cases: many clients opening parallel short-lived connections can effectively sidestep single-token smoothing. We'll need to canonicalize by api-key + enforce per-key session smoothing. Also consider a small per-tenant concurrency cap.

Sam: Rollout plan idea: dual-path mode where AdmissionService.Check consults (old_reservoir || new_watermark) controlled by tenant-hash. Start with 5% canary, monitor rejections and latency. A/B avoids big surprises.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary ingress rule applied: watermark-policy v1 -> 5% tenants at 2026-03-21T14:12Z :rocket:

Mira: Security/scale notes: watermark shards must be TTL'd for inactive tenants. Persisted state should be compact (float + ts) and transmitted over mTLS. Also make sure encryption of state when offloaded to store.

Alex: Proposed AdmissionService interface (minimal):
```
AdmissionService.Check(api_key, tenant_id, tokens_requested, priority, metadata) -> {
  admit: bool,
  reason: string,            # e.g. "watermark_exceeded", "spike_allowed"
  spike_allowance_used: int
}
```

Sam: Addendum: include an optional 'override_token' param for platform ops with auditing so we can trace exceptions.

Chen: Testing: we should create synthetic profiles: steady, bursty, churning parallel clients. Run perf tests to validate memory/CPU vs reservoir.

Mira: I'll own telemetry dashboards + alerts: p50/ p95 rejection rates, spike budget depletion per tenant, and a global alert if >0.1% of tenants hit sustained rejections.

Alex: Action items: 1) I'll write a short RFC that defines the watermark math, config knobs, and migration plan. 2) @Mira to spec telemetry dashboards. 3) @Chen to prototype per-key smoothing and concurrency cap. 4) @Sam to add priority-exception API + tests. Please review RFC by EOD Thursday. :thumbsup:

Sam: SGTM — will add test checklist to RFC.

Mira: On it, will comment in RFC with metric names and thresholds.
